newsitem.title: USA: Budget bill not seen ending interstate meat ban.
newsitem.headline: Budget bill not seen ending interstate meat ban.

text.p: U.S. Sen. Larry Pressler, R-S.D., was still working to get an amendment to lift a ban on interstate shipment of state-inspected meat and poultry into an omnibus budget bill on Monday, a Pressler aide said.
But the amendment was not part of the package being discussed on the Senate floor, and any additions to the bill at such a late stage "would be the exception rather than the rule," the aide said.
The version of the bill passed by the House of Representatives Saturday did not contain the measure, the aide said.
Small meat packers, who say federal inspection is too expensive, want to be allowed to ship their state-inspected meat and poultry to other states.
Consumer groups have said that, although states must by law inspect meat to equivalent standards as federal inspection, in many states the inspection is not so rigorous.
U.S. Agriculture Department has said that states must implement the new Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points regulations before the ban on interstate shipment is lifted.
